html:
The Chicago Boys were Chilean economists trained at the University of Chicago, many under Milton Friedman, who ran economic policy under the Pinochet dictatorship from 1975.

Under an exchange begun in the 1950s, students from Chile's Catholic University studied free-market economics in Chicago. After the coup, they cut tariffs, sold state companies, freed prices and in 1981 replaced the state pension system with private accounts. Inflation fell, but a banking crash in 1982 threw a third of workers out of jobs.

After 1985 Chile grew fast, and its model was copied in Eastern Europe and elsewhere, before such ideas were called neoliberalism. Critics blame it for deep inequality and weak public services, the anger behind the protests of 2019. It was part of the long rule of Pinochet.
sum: The Chicago Boys were Chilean economists trained at the University of Chicago, many under Milton Friedman, who ran economic policy under the Pinochet dictatorship from 1975.
